 Bidois brothers prepare to face each other in Saturday’s Kiwi Classico
 posted in: A-League (Men) , News , Uncategorized 
 | 
 Brothers Riley and Jonty Bidois will put family loyalties aside when they line up for opposing teams in Saturday’s men’s A-League derby. 
 The Tauranga-raised forwards are preparing to face each other competitively for the first time when Auckland FC host Wellington Phoenix at Go Media Stadium.
 Older brother Riley (24) represents the Phoenix, while Jonty plays for Auckland FC, adding a family rivalry to the seventh Kiwi Classico. Jonty turned 22 on Thursday.
 The brothers discussed their impending meeting with presenter James Dodd on the A-League’s online show On The Whistle .
 Main photo: Jonty Bidois and Riley Bidois … brother v brother.  
 “We’re excited,” Riley said.
 “I mean it’s gonna be a big occasion and all our family and friends are gonna be there.”
 Jonty said the prospect of becoming opponents had never featured in their childhood ambitions.
 “Yeah, we always talked about playing together one day, but I’m not gonna lie, I don’t think we’ve said like what happens if we play against each other!”
 Both brothers have been fielding requests for tickets from family and friends, although their family WhatsApp group has remained unusually quiet.
 Asked who their family would support, Jonty told On The Whistle : “I think they’re pretty neutral to be honest!”
 The brothers grew up supporting Wellington Phoenix, who were New Zealand’s only professional club before Auckland FC joined the competition in 2024.
 Riley recalled receiving tickets to watch the Phoenix for his 13th birthday, never imagining both brothers would eventually become professional footballers.
 Both brothers established themselves in senior football with Northern League club Tauranga City.
 Riley joined Wellington on loan from United States club Monterey Bay and scored with his first touch against Melbourne Victory in October.
 Jonty has established himself in Auckland’s squad, helping the club win last season’s men’s A-League championship.
 The Phoenix head into Saturday’s match with three wins from three games, while Auckland have won all six previous derbies.
 For the Bidois family, Saturday guarantees at least one disappointed son.
